title: A Liberal Education and Corruption of the Youths of Singapore
what_it_is: A Liberal Education and Corruption of the Youths of Singapore

sections.label: Singapore Climate Rally at Hong Lim
sections.summary: On 21 September, the Singapore Climate Rally gathered over 1,700 mostly youth participants at Hong Lim Park, peacefully calling for societal and economic restructuring to prevent climate change.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, on 21 September, the Singapore Climate Rally gathered more than 1,700 participants, most of them youths, to Hong Lim Park.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They peacefully called for Singapore to restructure our society and economy to prevent climate change.

sections.label: Activism compatible with academic role
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Minister's statement that activism is compatible with the academic role if the roles are appropriately separated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As for academics, I welcome the Minister’s statement that activism is compatible with the role of the academic, provided those roles are appropriately separated.

sections.label: Concern over academics teaching contentious topics
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned Singaporean academics will find it difficult to examine and teach contentious topics because standards must always be exacting, lest they be accused of subversion, flawed scholarship or activist motivations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What concerns me is that it will become difficult for Singaporean academics to examine and teach contentious topics because the standards must always be exacting, perfect, lest one is accused of subversion, flawed scholarship or activist motivations.

sections.label: Core Curriculum and liberal education
sections.summary: Almost all autonomous university programmes include Core Curriculum components exposing students to critical reading, writing and thinking, but the most comprehensive liberal education components remain reserved for the elite.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, almost all our autonomous university (AU) programmes have included Core Curriculum components that do expose students to critical reading, writing and thinking.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the most comprehensive components of a liberal education are still reserved for the elite.

sections.label: Ministry as convenor for liberal education
sections.summary: The Ministry could act as convenor, providing a safe space for autonomous university staff to share liberal education practices and signalling that liberal education is a foundation for lifelong learning and citizenship, not an elite luxury.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What the Ministry could do is to play a role as convenor, to provide a safe space for staff from our AUs to share their practices in liberal education and to send a message that liberal education is not a luxury for the elite but is, in fact, a foundation for lifelong learning and citizenship that as many as possible 	should receive.

sections.label: Speaking time under Standing Orders
sections.summary: Under the Standing Orders, Assoc Prof Walter Theseira had 20 minutes for the speech, and 10 minutes of speaking time remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Under the Standing Orders, Assoc Prof Walter Theseira had 20 minutes for the speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: You have 10 minutes of the speaking time left.

sections.label: Youth advocacy and NUS reforms
sections.summary: Youth courage and advocacy, including Monica Baey and 400 students, led to real policy reforms at NUS on sexual harassment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: For example, during the NUS controversy on sexual harassment, it was the courage and advocacy of youths that resulted in real policy reforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: If not for Monica Baey's courage to call out injustice, if not for the many students who pushed for a town hall, if not for the 400 students who turned up to confront their university administrators, it is unlikely that we would have seen change.

sections.label: Reinventing Youth Action Plan
sections.summary: Youths must be genuinely heard, with the Youth Action Plan reinvented to involve them in policymaking from feedback to testing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: To address this asymmetry, our youths must know they are genuinely heard.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: This includes reinventing the Youth Action Plan to go beyond providing grants and remodelling Somerset, to involving youths in the mechanism of policymaking, from feedback to testing and finetuning policies.

sections.label: Tommy Koh on loving critics
sections.summary: Prof Tommy Koh called for welcoming criticism from those who love Singapore, saying Singapore needs loving critics and critical lovers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Last week, our very own Ambassador-at-Large Prof Tommy Koh made a similar call for change to our fourth Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: He said, “We should welcome criticism as long as the critic loves Singapore and is not out to destroy Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Singapore will languish if its lovers are uncritical and its critics are unloving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: What Singapore needs is not sycophants but loving critics and critical lovers.” Loving critics and critical lovers must be given space to grow and thrive and be recognised for their value and importance to our society.

sections.label: Activism incompatible with academic role
sections.summary: An academic agrees that in the classroom, activism is incompatible with an academic's role of critically assessing issues from different perspectives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: First, as an academic myself, I agree with the Member that, in the classroom, activism is incompatible with the role of an academic, if one is to be able to critically assess issues from different perspectives.

sections.label: Academics should not mobilise support
sections.summary: Academics may hold their own views but should not mobilise support for partisan causes while teaching and mentoring students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Academics can hold their own views on various issues but they should not mobilise support for partisan causes in the course of teaching and mentoring students.

sections.label: Universities must follow Singapore laws
sections.summary: Minister Ong Ye Kung said universities based in Singapore must operate within Singapore's laws and recognise its social and cultural context.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Third, as Minister Ong Ye Kung said earlier, our universities, being based in Singapore, must operate within Singapore's laws and recognise our particular social and cultural context, like everyone else.

sections.label: Youth Conversations on key topics
sections.summary: The Youth Conversations heard over 8,000 youths on topics including social inequality, mental health, environmental sustainability and narratives of success.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, we started the Youth Conversations, hearing over 8,000 youths on topics that matter most to them, such as social inequality, mental health, environmental sustainability and narratives of success.

sections.label: Youth awareness and SG Youth Action Plan
sections.summary: Most participants reported better understanding of Singapore's issues and different views, leading to the SG Youth Action Plan for concrete action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Among those who participated, 80% of youths indicated a better understanding of issues that Singapore faces and close to 90% agreed that they became more aware of different views.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The next stage would be to prepare our youths to take concrete action for positive change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This is why we started the SG Youth Action Plan.
